newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound Palestinian in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound Palestinian in Gaza.

text.p: An Israeli army patrol at a Jewish settlement block in the Gaza Strip shot and wounded one Palestinian in the leg overnight, Israeli military sources said on Thursday.

They said the patrol at the Gush Katif settlement saw two Palestinians near the settlement area's fence and called on them to halt. When the two did not respond, the patrol fired in the air and then at the two men, wounding one of them.
The sources said both Palestinians fled to territory under Palestinian Authority jurisdiction.

The shooting came amidst rising tensions over a three-month impasse in PLO-Israeli peace moves and expansion of Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip.
In the West Bank town of Hebron on Wednesday, Israeli soldiers shot and wounded three Palestinians in a fifth straight day of clashes with stone-throwing Arabs, witnesses said.

Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule under an interim peace deal in January but kept troops in the heart of the city to protect some 400 Jews who have settled there in fortified enclaves.
Hebron is home to more than 100,000 Palestinians. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accused the Palestinian Authority of orchestrating the unrest. The Authority rejects the charge.
